title: Data Structures & Algorithms
description: Practical data structures and algorithms reference covering complexity, arrays, strings, linked lists, stacks, queues, hash tables, trees, heaps, tries, graphs, sorting, searching, recursion, dynamic programming, greedy methods, backtracking, union-find, and algorithm selection.

subtopics.title: Time, Space & Amortized Complexity
subtopics.description: Analyze dominant growth in input parameters, distinguish worst/average/amortized bounds, and include auxiliary memory, recursion depth, preprocessing, and output size.

callouts.title: Big-O Hides Constants and Hardware
callouts.text: Cache locality, allocation, hashing, vectorization, branch behavior, I/O, and input distribution can dominate realistic ranges. Benchmark representative workloads after selecting a sound complexity class.

subtopics.title: Arrays, Dynamic Arrays & Strings
subtopics.description: Arrays provide contiguous indexed storage; dynamic arrays grow amortized; strings may be bytes, code units, or Unicode scalar/grapheme sequences depending on language.

callouts.title: Define What a Character Means
callouts.text: Byte indexing, Unicode code points, and user-perceived grapheme clusters differ. Choose representation and normalization from the problem.

subtopics.title: Linked Lists, Stacks, Queues & Deques
subtopics.description: Linked lists support local insertion with node access but have poor locality; stacks are LIFO, queues FIFO, and deques support both ends.

callouts.title: An Array-Based Container Is Often Faster
callouts.text: Even with similar asymptotics, contiguous memory, fewer allocations, and simpler iteration usually favor dynamic arrays/deques unless stable nodes or local splicing is essential.

subtopics.title: Hash Tables & Sets
subtopics.description: Hash tables offer expected constant-time lookup with a good hash and controlled load factor; collision strategy, resizing, key equality, and adversarial input affect behavior.

codeBlocks.code:
map[key] → hash → bucket/index → equality check
Average lookup/insert/delete: O(1)
Worst case: O(n) without collision protections
Set operations: membership, dedupe, intersection, union
Design key: immutable equality/hash semantics

callouts.title: Hash Iteration Is Usually Unordered
callouts.text: Do not rely on incidental iteration order. Sort keys or use an ordered structure when deterministic output is a contract.

subtopics.title: Binary Search Trees, Balanced Trees & Tries
subtopics.description: Balanced search trees maintain ordered keys with logarithmic operations; tries index sequences by prefixes and trade memory for prefix operations.

callouts.title: Tree Shape Depends on Invariants
callouts.text: Saying 'tree lookup is O(log n)' requires balance or other structural guarantees. A plain BST can become a linked list.

subtopics.title: Heaps & Priority Queues
subtopics.description: A binary heap provides O(1) peek and O(log n) insertion/removal of the extreme element, ideal for scheduling, top-k, shortest-path frontiers, and streaming selection.

codeBlocks.code:
Binary min-heap invariant: parent <= children
peek min: O(1)
push: append + sift up → O(log n)
pop min: swap root/last + remove + sift down → O(log n)
build heap from n items: O(n), not O(n log n)

callouts.title: A Heap Is Not Fully Sorted
callouts.text: Only the root is guaranteed extreme. Searching for an arbitrary value remains O(n) unless an auxiliary index is maintained.

subtopics.title: Graph Representation, BFS & DFS
subtopics.description: Adjacency lists suit sparse graphs, matrices suit dense constant-time edge checks. BFS discovers shortest unweighted path layers; DFS explores depth and supports cycle/topological components.

callouts.title: Track Visited at the Correct Time
callouts.text: Marking only after dequeue/recursion can enqueue the same node many times. The exact timing depends on whether multiple paths/results must be preserved.

subtopics.title: Sorting & Selection
subtopics.description: Choose sorting by stability, comparison/key model, memory, input distribution, parallelism, and whether all elements or only top-k are required.

rows: Average O(n log n), worst O(n²)

callouts.title: Use the Standard Library Sort
callouts.text: Production library implementations are highly tuned and tested. Implement sorting manually for learning or specialized proven constraints.

subtopics.title: Binary Search, Two Pointers & Sliding Windows
subtopics.description: Binary search applies to a monotonic predicate, not only arrays. Two-pointer and sliding-window methods exploit ordered movement or maintain an incremental contiguous range.

codeBlocks.code:
Binary search invariant:
  lo = definitely false region boundary
  hi = definitely true region boundary
  while gap remains: mid → evaluate monotonic predicate → shrink

Sliding window:
  expand right → update state
  while invalid: remove left → advance
  record best/count when invariant holds

callouts.title: Write the Boundary Invariant First
callouts.text: Most binary-search bugs come from mixing inclusive/exclusive bounds, midpoint rules, and return meanings. State what lo and hi represent before coding.

subtopics.title: Recursion, Divide-and-Conquer & Backtracking
subtopics.description: Recursion needs a shrinking measure and base case. Divide-and-conquer combines independent subproblems; backtracking explores choices while undoing state and pruning impossible branches.

codeBlocks.code:
backtrack(state):
  if complete: record solution; return
  for candidate in choices(state):
    if violates constraints: continue
    apply(candidate)
    backtrack(state)
    undo(candidate)

Prune with bounds, ordering, memoized dead states, symmetry breaking

callouts.title: Recursion Depth Is a Resource
callouts.text: Deep input can overflow call stacks. Convert to an explicit stack/queue or enforce depth limits for untrusted trees and graphs.

subtopics.title: Dynamic Programming, Greedy Methods & Union-Find
subtopics.description: DP caches overlapping subproblems with an explicit state and recurrence; greedy algorithms require an exchange/invariant proof; union-find maintains disjoint components efficiently.

codeBlocks.code:
DP recipe: define state → recurrence → base cases → evaluation order → reconstruct
Memoization: top-down, reachable states only, recursion overhead
Tabulation: bottom-up, predictable memory/order
Greedy: choose local option only with proof it preserves optimum
Union-find: parent + rank/size + path compression ≈ amortized constant

callouts.title: Do Not Use DP Without Defining State
callouts.text: State must contain exactly the information needed for future decisions. Missing state makes recurrence wrong; excess state causes unnecessary complexity.

subtopics.title: Selection, Correctness & Checklist
subtopics.description: Start from constraints and required output, derive invariants, choose structures that make dominant operations cheap, prove termination/correctness, and test edge/adversarial cases.

codeBlocks.code:
1. Clarify n, ranges, duplicates, ordering, mutability, memory, streaming
2. Work examples and define output precisely
3. Establish brute-force baseline
4. Identify repeated work/monotonicity/order/graph/state
5. Select data structure + invariant + complexity
6. Test empty, one, duplicate, sorted, reverse, overflow, huge/adversarial
7. Benchmark representative data when constants matter

callouts.title: Production Checklist
callouts.text: State complexity in all input dimensions, account for memory/output, preserve invariants, use standard containers/algorithms, handle Unicode/numeric overflow, bound adversarial work, test properties and edge cases, and profile before micro-optimizing.
